issues.title: Order total is off by a cent on some orders
issues.body: `orders/total.py` sums floats and rounds with `round`, so 3 × 0.35 gives 1.05 on one order and 1.04 on another. Done when the total rounds half up, in Decimal.

issues.title: Export the orders of a month as CSV
issues.body: The shop owner needs the orders of a month as a CSV file: order, customer, total.

issues.body: The admin pages have only a light theme.

issues.title: The docstring of vat says cents, but it returns euros
issues.body:
`billing/tax.py:4`: the docstring of `vat` says "Returns the VAT on amount, in cents." The function returns euros: a `Decimal` quantized to `0.01`. Its only caller, `get_invoice_total` in `billing/invoice.py:5`, adds the result to an order total in euros.

A reader who trusts the docstring can divide the result by 100, or multiply a caller's value by 100, and get a wrong invoice total.

Fix: say "in euros, rounded to the cent" in the docstring.

Out of scope for #14 Order total is off by a cent on some orders: that fix changes `orders/`, and this is in `billing/`.

issues.title: Sign-up treats emails that differ only in case as two accounts
issues.body:
`accounts/signup.py:4`: `sign_up` checks and stores the email exactly as typed. So `Bob@shop.test` and `bob@shop.test` sign up as two accounts for the same mailbox.

Steps:

```python
from accounts.signup import sign_up
sign_up("bob@shop.test", "h1")
sign_up("Bob@shop.test", "h2")  # no ValueError: a second account
```

Expected: the second call raises `ValueError("this email has an account")`.

A likely fix compares and stores a normalized email (for example `email.strip().lower()`). Which normalization to use is a product decision: the local part of an address is case-sensitive by the standard, though almost no provider treats it so. The login lookup must use the same normalization.

Out of scope for #14 Order total is off by a cent on some orders: that fix changes `orders/`, and this is in `accounts/`.
